TraceContract.purpose: Define the cross-module observability identifiers and the BLOCK_* marker grammar that lets verification scenarios assert both outcome correctness and trajectory correctness from captured stderr/log output. Schema is decoupled from runtime: every M-XXX module ships eprintln! markers conforming to this grammar today, and a future tracing-layer crate (Phase-B1) will harvest them into structured events without changing the on-the-wire format consumed by tests.

trace_id.semantics: One per process invocation. Time-ordered so trace archives sort naturally. Survives until process exit.
trace_id.emission: Appended automatically by Phase-B1 tracing layer; not present in eprintln! markers today.

req_id.semantics: One per renderer→main IPC roundtrip. Renderer generates; main echoes back unchanged in both ack and event fanout payloads.
req_id.emission: Phase-B3 (M-013a/M-013b IPC bridge); not present today (no IPC layer yet).

session_chain_id.semantics: Identifies a window+renderer session. Survives in- process IPC chain; resets per new window. Used to correlate renderer-side console with main-side events.
session_chain_id.emission: Phase-B3 (M-001 window lifecycle hooks); not present today.

conventions.c: First segment of the Rust module path, lowercase, snake_case as already in source. Examples: legacy, dialog, migration_strings, mt_paths, cancel_log, main. NOT the M-XXX ID — markers stay grep-friendly without cross-referencing the module catalog.
Function name OR a named logical block within a function (chosen when one function emits multiple distinct milestones). Snake-case.

SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE noun describing the milestone. Names are unique across the codebase — never repeat a BLOCK_NAME in different modules even if their domains differ; use suffixes (e.g. BLOCK_LEGACY_FOUND, BLOCK_DIALOG_OPEN) instead.

SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE noun describing an error/abort/coercion. The `MT_` prefix is reserved for non-milestone identifiers that cross module boundaries — typically defined as a `pub const` in the producing module (e.g. MT_PREFS_V1_RUNNING in prefs.rs) and embedded in the call site's emit marker. Distinct namespace from BLOCK_*; tests assert against the exact byte string for stability.
Optional inline structured fields. Stable key names; values quoted only when whitespace is present. Avoid logging anything matching token regexes or path-leaking PII.

edge-cases.ec: Symlink loop A→B→A: readlink chain bounded; returns MT_FS_SYMLINK_LOOP after N=40 hops (matches POSIX ELOOP).
Broken symlink (target deleted): stat returns MT_FS_BROKEN_LINK; read does NOT fall back to creating target.
Symlink pointing outside sandbox root: canonicalize then re-validate against M-010; rejected BEFORE open(2).
Non-regular inode (FIFO, socket, block/char device, /dev/zero): S_ISREG check fails → MT_FS_NOT_REGULAR. Must not block on read from FIFO.
Filename containing NUL byte (`foo\0bar`) or path separator inside segment: rejected at BLOCK_VALIDATE_PATH (pre-CString conversion).
Windows reserved names (CON, PRN, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9) with or without extension: rejected on Windows target only; allowed on Unix.
Trailing whitespace / trailing dot filenames on Windows: rejected (NTFS silently strips, causing write-vs-read path mismatch).
Disk-full mid-write: write(2) returns ENOSPC → atomic temp+rename contract ensures original file untouched; temp cleaned up.
fsync ordering: write-to-temp → fsync(temp) → rename → fsync(parent-dir). All four syscalls observable via strace/dtruss.
Read-only parent directory: creating new file returns EACCES → MT_FS_PERM_DENIED; no partial file left.
macOS TCC denial (Desktop/Documents/Downloads without entitlement): errno 1 EPERM → stable MT_FS_TCC_DENIED distinct from MT_FS_PERM_DENIED.
External mv/rm between validate_path and open: open returns ENOENT → MT_FS_RACE_VANISHED (not MT_FS_NOT_FOUND) so UI can refresh.

On ENOSPC during write, original file SHA256 unchanged after error; exactly one BLOCK_ATOMIC_RENAME failure log.
Symlink loop emits exactly one BLOCK_RESOLVE_SYMLINK with hops==40 then error — not 40 separate logs.

edge-cases.ec: UTF-8 truncated at chunk boundary mid-codepoint (`\xE2\x98` of `\xE2\x98\x83` ☃): detector must defer decision or buffer tail — never misclassify as Latin-1.
Overlong UTF-8 (`\xC0\x80` for NUL): rejected as invalid UTF-8, does NOT roundtrip.
Unpaired UTF-16 surrogate (`\xD8\x00` LE without low surrogate): flagged MT_ENC_INVALID_SURROGATE; not silently replaced with U+FFFD in strict mode.
BOM masquerade: UTF-16LE BOM (`\xFF\xFE`) prefix on otherwise UTF-8 bytes: BOM wins, decoded as UTF-16LE; emits BLOCK_DETECT_BOM with bom="utf-16le".
0-byte file: returns default encoding (UTF-8) with BOM=none, newline=LF; no chardet call.
1-byte file (`A`): chardet low-confidence → fallback UTF-8 deterministically (not random).
File containing only BOM (3 bytes EF BB BF): treated as UTF-8 empty; write-back preserves BOM if user didn't toggle.
Latin-1 vs Windows-1252 vs MacRoman vs ISO-8859-15: bytes `\x80\x99\xA4` decode differently; fixture per codec; chardet confidence + tiebreak rule logged at BLOCK_CHARDET_GUESS.
CP932 vs CP936 vs CP949: same high-byte pair decodes to Japanese/Chinese/Korean; assertion pins detector output per fixture (not "any of three").
Mixed encoding (first 1KB UTF-8 + second 1KB Shift-JIS): detector returns majority or MT_ENC_MIXED; decoder either fails fast or produces U+FFFD with marker BLOCK_DECODE_REPLACEMENT { count }.
CRLF detection with CR byte mid-UTF-16 codepoint (`\x0D\x00` = U+000D, not a line break): newline detector runs on DECODED text, not raw bytes.
File content in NFC vs NFD: byte-roundtrip preserves original form (no silent NFC re-normalization). SHA256 in == SHA256 out when no edit.
Right-to-left override U+202E embedded in content: decoded faithfully, but render layer warned via BLOCK_BIDI_OVERRIDE_DETECTED; filename with U+202E rejected at M-002 validate_path.
BOM-smuggling: invisible ZWNBSP (U+FEFF) not at offset 0 is NOT treated as BOM (only byte-0 prefix counts); assertion prevents false strip.

negative-assertions.no: 0-byte and 1-byte fixtures: zero BLOCK_CHARDET_GUESS beyond 1 call; deterministic output across 100 runs.
ZWNBSP at offset >0: zero BLOCK_DETECT_BOM with bom="utf-8"; byte unchanged.
NFC↔NFD: zero auto-normalization log markers; input_sha256 == output_sha256 on no-edit roundtrip.
Overlong/surrogate invalid sequences: zero "successful decode" path (BLOCK_DECODE_OK not emitted); error is stable code.

scenarios.scenario-3: mt::close-project-root from renderer pathname=/A: BLOCK_DISPATCH logged, win resolved via fromWebContents, editor.closeFolder('/A') invoked, which fires watcher-unwatch-directory for /A.
scenarios.scenario-4: mt::close-project-root for path not currently a project root: editor.closeFolder no-op or returns falsy; BLOCK_NOOP_UNKNOWN_PATH logged; no throw.
scenarios.scenario-5: mt::close-project-root from destroyed sender: fromWebContents returns null; BLOCK_SKIP_DEAD_WINDOW logged; no exception.
scenarios.scenario-6: Watcher payload contract: mt::update-object-tree body = {type, change:{pathname,...}}; no rootId/rootPathname/windowId added by main.

edge-cases.ec: Two watcher-watch-directory IPCs for SAME path in same window: current Watcher.watch does NOT dedup — allocates fresh uniqueId, double events. Surface as enforced dedup at watcher.js (preferred) OR renderer reducer; mark KNOWN-GAP if neither.

chokidar fails to spawn (EACCES, ENOENT race, ENOSPC): watcher.js handles ENOSPC explicitly; others log only. Verify entry remains in watchers map post-error so unwatch can clear; no zombie/orphan FDs.
Multi-window: window 1 watches /A, window 2 watches /B. unwatchByWindowId filter on w.win.id; watch() captures per-call win in closure. Events from /A's chokidar always go to window 1.
50 roots, close 49: Object.keys(watchers).length===1; lsof delta ≈0 vs single-root baseline (modulo polling fds on macOS).
Renderer 1 sends mt::close-project-root with path actually a root of Renderer 2: handler scopes by sender window; editor.closeFolder treats unknown-to-this-window path as no-op.
Window closes mid-flight: window-closed listener calls unwatchByWindowId before deleting; in-flight close-project-root then BLOCK_SKIP_DEAD_WINDOW or BLOCK_NOOP_UNKNOWN_PATH; no double-close.

negative-assertions.no: MUST NOT call unwatchByWindowId from mt::close-project-root or watcher-unwatch-directory handler — only single-path unwatch permitted.
MUST NOT route watcher events from window 1's chokidar to window 2's webContents.
MUST NOT trust pathname payload as cross-window scope key — scope from BrowserWindow.fromWebContents(e.sender).
MUST NOT throw if chokidar instance already gone.
MUST NOT add per-root tagging / rootId / aggregation to mt::update-object-tree payloads.
MUST NOT register mt::close-project-root outside _listenForIpcMain or more than once.

V-M-901.intent: Verify that AI Standards token/session hygiene is adopted only as a GRACE-compatible overlay and cannot bypass contracts, knowledge graph updates, or required verification.

module-checks.check-2: rg "correctness > required verification|correctness > required verification" docs/grace-ai-standards-hygiene-methodology.md docs/development-plan.xml

scenarios.scenario-1: Small localized doc/code task uses targeted context only after contract, KG, and verification references are identified.
scenarios.scenario-2: Security, migration, shared API, or architectural drift forces wave/full context even when token budget is high.
scenarios.scenario-3: If a worker proposes skipping verification for economy, GH_VERIFICATION_SKIPPED blocks execution.

edge-cases.ec: A task that touches docs/verification-plan.xml must not be treated as read-only context optimization.
Security modules require full or wave context regardless of token economy.
Data migration modules require old/new schema and rollback evidence loaded together.
Scoped review may start targeted but must escalate if dependency boundary is unclear.
Large artifact loading may be summarized, but source-of-truth excerpts must remain precise.

negative-assertions.no: MUST NOT replace GRACE XML artifacts with Markdown-only policy.
MUST NOT allow token economy to overrule required verification.

V-M-902.intent: Verify operational packets expose context hygiene decisions explicitly, including what was loaded, what was skipped, why, and whether verification remained mandatory.

scenarios.scenario-1: ExecutionPacket includes enough context to execute one module without loading unrelated modules.
scenarios.scenario-2: Packet with skipped verification and no blocker is rejected.
scenarios.scenario-3: Reviewer can reconstruct scope decisions from packet fields alone.

edge-cases.ec: Skipped artifact references must be concrete file paths or module IDs, not vague prose.
If dependency summaries are stale, packet validation escalates to graph refresh.
additional-context-needed must block execution until resolved.
Parallel workers may use different targeted packets but must share the same graph baseline.
Security packets must record redaction and secret-handling constraints.

negative-assertions.no: MUST NOT omit verification-excerpt when module checks exist.
MUST NOT hide unknowns inside notes instead of context-risk.

V-M-903.intent: Verify session handoffs preserve exact continuation state across compaction, agent rotation, and paused execution.

scenarios.scenario-1: Compacted summary names current task, changed files, verification status, blockers, and next exact action.
scenarios.scenario-2: Resume detects stale decision or missing blocker and pauses before editing.
scenarios.scenario-3: Swarm continuation keeps independent reviewer/verifier findings separate until orchestration merge.

edge-cases.ec: Dirty worktree files not owned by the current task are recorded and not reverted.
Handoff after failed verification includes first divergent block and observed evidence.
Handoff for plan-only work explicitly says no source code changed.
Multiple subagent outputs are deduplicated only by orchestrator, not by individual workers.
Handoff is compact, but every claim points to a concrete file or command.

negative-assertions.no: MUST NOT resume from memory when handoff contradicts current git status.
MUST NOT mark verification passed without command/evidence names.

V-M-904.intent: Verify GRACE skills have explicit context defaults and escalation rules that preserve strict review and verification quality.

scenarios.scenario-1: $grace-execute uses targeted packets for one module after canonical artifacts are loaded by controller.
scenarios.scenario-2: $grace-reviewer starts scoped but escalates on architecture, security, migration, or graph ambiguity.
scenarios.scenario-3: $grace-verification may summarize unrelated suites but cannot omit critical path gates.

edge-cases.ec: Reviewer scope cannot stay targeted for secret-handling, sandbox, or updater signature changes.
Verification must load both legacy and target schema references for migration tasks.
Refresh must inspect KG, development plan, and verification plan together when node edges changed.
Independent swarm outputs must not share a pre-deduplicated finding list.
Plan phase may summarize code but must read requirements/technology/verification intent.

negative-assertions.no: MUST NOT downgrade mandatory swarm review/verification because of token budget.
MUST NOT treat skill instructions as replacing project AGENTS.md rules.

V-M-905.intent: Verify hygiene gates catch false passes, undeclared skips, and insufficient context before execution continues.

scenarios.scenario-1: A packet with verification-not-skipped=false and no blocker fails Gate-Phase-H.
scenarios.scenario-2: A targeted context decision on a shared contract edit without dependency summaries fails.
scenarios.scenario-3: A properly scoped packet with concrete skipped-artifacts rationale passes hygiene verification.

edge-cases.ec: Review says "no issues" but did not inspect verification excerpt; gate fails.
Source code changed without MODULE_CONTRACT or MODULE_MAP update; hygiene cannot excuse it.
New module added without KG node; gate fails even if tests pass.
Large logs may be sampled, but required markers must be searched deterministically.
Redaction and secret logging checks cannot be skipped as expensive.

negative-assertions.no: MUST NOT mark a verification skip as pass.
MUST NOT accept "not relevant" without module/flow evidence.

V-M-906.intent: Verify context hygiene modules are discoverable in KG while remaining meta-process modules, not Mark Text runtime modules.

scenarios.scenario-1: KG navigation from M-901 reaches packet, handoff, skill-scope, verification, and graph hygiene modules.
scenarios.scenario-2: M-901..M-906 paths point to docs artifacts only, not src/ or src-tauri/ runtime code.

Reviewer can find the methodology from KG without scanning all docs.

V-M-013a.intent: Verify the typed IPC contract layer owns command names, payload schemas, generated TypeScript, listener lifecycle, and req_id correlation without relying on runtime backend implementations.

scenarios.scenario-1: Generated Tauri v2 command-name fixture has empty symmetric difference against pinned Electron v1 fixture unless an explicit documented exception exists.
scenarios.scenario-2: Every generated command payload type compiles with zero `any` exports in the contract package.
scenarios.scenario-3: Ten concurrent correlated requests with out-of-order replies resolve by req_id, not arrival order.
scenarios.scenario-4: HMR and component unmount leave listener refcount stable after 50 attach/detach cycles.

edge-cases.ec: Unknown command rejects with MT_IPC_UNKNOWN_COMMAND and never silently drops.
Schema drift between Rust serde/ts-rs and committed TypeScript fails CI.
1KB invoke p95 <5ms intra-process; listener attach/detach amortized <1ms.
Aborted request rejects E_WINDOW_GONE and does not resolve later.
Contract package exposes no raw `invoke(name, any)` escape hatch to production renderer code.

negative-assertions.no: MUST NOT import @electron/remote or use ipcRenderer.sendSync.
MUST NOT commit generated TypeScript drift after codegen.
MUST NOT use `any` in public IPC contract exports.

V-M-013b.intent: Verify the runtime IPC facade maps Electron-era channels to Tauri commands/events, returns MT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED for pending wave stubs, and preserves command parity through B2/B3 growth.

scenarios.scenario-1: On boot, registered runtime command names match the committed Tauri fixture; mismatch emits BLOCK_VALIDATE_AGAINST_FIXTURE and fails fast.
scenarios.scenario-2: Pending fs/search/watch commands return Err(MT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED), never panic, during partial B2 waves.
scenarios.scenario-3: Clipboard/window/context-menu replacements cover all six @electron/remote call-site categories.
scenarios.scenario-4: Open-file replay waits for both WebView readiness and listener registration, then delivers exactly once.
scenarios.scenario-5: Gate-B3a production bundle has zero sendSync and zero @electron/remote references.

edge-cases.ec: Unknown runtime channel returns MT_IPC_UNKNOWN_CHANNEL with bundle version and channel name.
Queued replay into a closed window is dropped with a marker, not delivered to stale state.
Runtime facade may depend on M-013a and backend modules; backend modules must not import the frontend facade.
No @electron/remote bridge remains in production code after Gate-B3a.
1MB payload threshold rejects oversize requests deterministically.

negative-assertions.no: MUST NOT panic for unimplemented wave stubs.
MUST NOT silently drop unknown channels.
MUST NOT leave dynamic response channel names without req_id correlation.
MUST NOT expose raw native menu/window APIs to renderer outside typed facade.

V-M-021.intent: Verify the internal filesystem primitive layer provides TOCTOU-safe validated paths, raw-byte IO, atomic writes, trash-only delete semantics, and bounded concurrency for all Rust-internal callers.

scenarios.scenario-1: Symlink-swap after validation but before read is blocked by held fd and post-open canonical path verification.
scenarios.scenario-2: SIGKILL between rename and dir-fsync leaves original SHA256 unchanged or recoverable temp state.
scenarios.scenario-3: Trash unavailable returns MT_FS_CORE_TRASH_UNAVAILABLE and never hard-unlinks as fallback.
scenarios.scenario-4: Two simultaneous writes to the same path serialize through per-path mutex; final file is one complete payload.
scenarios.scenario-5: 10k file stat batch completes under 2s on M1 SSD and p99 single stat remains under 5ms.

edge-cases.ec: Reject Linux magic symlinks: /proc/self/root, /proc/<pid>/, /dev/fd/, /sys/.
macOS fcntl(F_GETPATH) post-open verification required before trusting canonical path.
Windows Defender locked file retries max 3 with 50ms backoff; no infinite retry.
Open-file semaphore caps fan-out at N=64.
Raw bytes are preserved; M-014 owns encoding decode/encode decisions.

negative-assertions.no: MUST NOT hard-delete when Trash is unavailable.
MUST NOT expose IPC commands directly; M-002 wraps M-021.
MUST NOT reopen paths after validation for the actual read/write.
MUST NOT log file contents or absolute home paths.

cache_root writes do not mutate legacy ~/Library/Application Support/marktext/ data.
Path helpers never include secrets or tokens in logs.
Path naming must be consistent between M-022 contract and Phase-B-pre2 implementation evidence.

MUST NOT write under protected legacy Application Support paths during preflight cancel logging.
